prose.summary: The product meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. This results in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED. See the checklist below for the required steps.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, described as Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal MFN rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. Claiming the CEPA rate yields an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED. This reduction applies only to Basic Customs Duty; other import charges such as IGST remain payable.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and at least 45% value addition (VA) on an FOB basis. The final manufacture check passed, meaning the last manufacturing step occurred in the UAE, and the minimal operations check passed, indicating the work goes beyond the simple operations that alone do not confer origin. The CTSH check passed because all three non‑originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010, and the VA check passed with a build‑down of 49.0% against the 45% threshold.

notes.text: The application must include the HS code, description, quantity and value, and each item must qualify separately. The customs authority may ask for cost sheets and a factory visit.
Refusing a verification visit can lead to denial of preferential benefits.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, whatever the product-specific rule says.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating.
Discrepancy between agreement and India's certificate form on box number; India's form governs entry into India.
The application must include HS code, description, quantity and value; each item must qualify separately; authority may ask for cost sheets and factory visit.
Refusing a verification visit is grounds for denying preferential benefits.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources.

The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD), and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II. IGST, GST compensation cess and the Social Welfare Surcharge still apply.
